subject: Security packet review and prioritization — next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <sam@heliolabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-01T10:12:00Z
Subject: Security packet + quick recap and next steps

Hi Samir / Emma —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about Helio Labs' product search use case and the throughput/latency targets you have for query-time reranking. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- What we heard: production traffic ~120 QPS peak, median sequence lengths ~64 tokens, primary region: US, some EU compliance needs.
- What Redwood can provide: hosted API for fast POC; Dedicated pools with VPC for production; SOC 2 evidence and retention controls.
- Immediate asks from your side: security packet review, legal confirmation on data residency and retention, and an internal decision on whether to pilot with Hosted or Dedicated.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Packet_v3.pdf (PDF) — includes SOC 2 report excerpt, network architecture, and data handling FAQ. Also attached SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf (one-page).

Proposed next steps:
1) Do a focused session with your security/infosec team if any details in the packet need clarifying (I can coordinate a 20-min slot next week).
2) If the packet looks good, we can spin up a 2-week POC on Hosted and share a mutual action plan with milestones.
3) If you prefer Dedicated from day one for isolation, we can put together an estimated timeline and cost.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the security review and whether a short Q&A session would help?

Thanks — I’ll follow up in a couple of days if I don’t hear back.

Best,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_Security_Packet_v3.pdf (PDF); SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf (PDF)

From: Samir Patel <sam@heliolabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@heliolabs.com>
Date: 2027-02-07T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick pulse on the security packet review (re: Security packet + quick recap and next steps)

Neha —

Thanks for the follow-up and for sending the packet. We did receive both PDFs. Quick update from Legal/Security: they’ve started a review but have a couple of items to clarify before we can move the pilot forward. High level:

- Data residency: we need confirmation that customer data processed via Redwood's hosted API remains in the selected region (US) and is not replicated to other regions for processing.
- Retention & logging: our legal team is asking for the default retention period for logs and what options we have to shorten it (ideally 30 days or less).
- Contract/POC terms: soft ask to see a short POC MSA template or a one-pager that outlines liability/SLAs for pilots.

We should be able to complete the review in ~10–14 business days unless these items require deeper architecture review. Could you provide concise answers to the three bullets above and attach the POC MSA or pointer to where we can review it? If a short call will speed this, Emma and I are available Thurs afternoon.

Appreciate it —
Samir
Head of Platform, Helio Labs
sam@heliolabs.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <sam@heliolabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T11:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick pulse on the security packet review (answers + MSA template)

Samir / Emma —

Thanks for the quick note and for outlining the review questions — really helpful. Answers below and I’ve attached a short POC MSA template for your legal team to scan.

1) Data residency: For Hosted API, requests from customers deployed in the US are processed in our US region only; we do not replicate customer inference traffic cross-region. If you require additional guarantees, our Dedicated deployment (VPC) provides an isolation model we can commit to in the SOW.

2) Retention & logging: Default request/trace logs are retained for 30 days. We can offer a policy to reduce retention to 7 or 14 days for pilots by configuration, and we support on-request purging of logs. Audit logs required for compliance are kept according to the retention schedule in the SOC2 summary (attached).

3) POC MSA: Attached is a one-page POC MSA (POC-MSA-Redwood.pdf) that covers pilot liability, data handling clauses, and a simple SLA for pilot throughput/availability. If you’d like, our legal ops can take a quick pass to remove any optional clauses to accelerate signature.

Attachments included: POC-MSA-Redwood.pdf (PDF); SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf (PDF)

Next steps I propose:
- If those responses look good, would you be open to a 20-minute call on Thursday at 3pm ET to walk through any remaining clarifying questions?
- I’ll loop in Rishi (cc’d) — he’s our product security lead and can join the call if you prefer.

If you confirm the time, I’ll send a calendar invite and include the short MSA in the invite for legal to comment inline.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a pilot.

Best,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: POC-MSA-Redwood.pdf (PDF); SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf (PDF)
